title: Thread Compressor — personal PRD sketch
content:
Quick brain-dump / scratchpad for a small product experiment: 'Thread Compressor'

Goal (one-liner): give apps a cheap way to preserve long conversational context at high fidelity for the last N turns while compressing older turns into a compact representation to reduce token cost and latency.

Problem assumptions / motivation:
- Many customers store entire chat history and re-send full context to model each turn; heavy token cost and tail latency for long sessions.
- Existing prefix caching helps only when prefixes are identical; multi-party or branching conversations still require re-sending tokens.
- Users care most about recent turns + salient facts; older background can be lossy-compressed.
- We can trade off fidelity for cost in a predictable way and expose knobs (window size, compression level).

Primary persona:
- PM/engineer embedding chat into a product (support agent, tutor app, collaborative doc assistant) who needs to keep session length unbounded while meeting cost and latency targets.

Success metrics (experiment):
- Per-session token reduction vs naive full-history (target: 4x reduction for sessions > 3k tokens)
- 99th-quantile response latency improvement on long sessions (target: -25% for >2k tokens)
- User-visible QA: percent of turns where compressed context caused a correctness regression (target: <3% on a curated eval set)
- CPU/GPU cost per 1k active sessions (estimate before/after)

User stories / flows:
1) As an engineer, I want an API that accepts a conversation and returns a compressed payload + metadata I can store and send later.
   - Input: list of messages {role, content, timestamp, id}
   - Output: compressed_blob (opaque base64), manifest {summary_tokens, anchors, last_n_raw_ids}
2) As an engineer, I want to call generate with a mixture of raw recent messages + a compressed_blob so the runtime can reconstruct context cheaply.
3) As an engineer, I want control over compression policy: aggressive/conservative, preserve-entities, preserve-qna, length cap.

Sketch: two API primitives
- POST /v1/threads/compress  (body: messages + policy) -> {compressed_blob, manifest}
- POST /v1/threads/expand-and-generate (body: recent_messages, compressed_blob, prompt_template, model) -> streaming response

Implementation ideas (fast prototype):
- Compression = hybrid: extractive + abstractive
  - Stage 1: lightweight extractive filter (heuristics + TF-IDF / embedding clustering) to pick salient sentences/turns (cheap)
  - Stage 2: abstractive summarizer (small instruct-tuned LLM on Redwood hosted) to produce a compact narrative + bullet anchors (100-200 tokens)
  - Store anchors + short embedding index for retrieval to reconstruct when needed
- Expansion at runtime: runtime merges recent raw tokens + expanded summary (optionally expand placeholders like user-specific facts by re-fetching small KV store)
- Cache compressed_blob as immutable; manifest includes approximation of info-loss (per-anchor score)

Quality control / eval pipeline (MVP):
- Create 200 session transcripts across three domains (support, tutoring, writing assistant)
- Compare full-context baseline vs compressor+expand pipeline across metrics: ROUGE, entailment-based correctness tests, and manual spot checks
- Flag common failure modes: copied code truncation, numeric tables, step-by-step instructions (these probably need policy: never-compress-blocks-within triple-backticks)

API UX notes (developer ergonomics):
- Keep compressed_blob opaque but allow opt-in transparency: offer small 'explain' endpoint that returns extracted anchors and the abstractive summary for debugging
- Provide SDK helpers to auto-manage rotation of last_n_raw_messages and to auto-call compress when session > token_threshold
- Telemetry: emit compression_rate, estimated_token_savings, expand_latency, model_used_for_summarization

Rollout plan (safe path):
- Alpha: internal teams + 2 pilot customers (enable via console flag), default policy conservative (preserve code blocks, preserve quoted messages, preserve entity lines)
- Observability: side-by-side traffic sampling (20% baseline full-history, 80% compressed) for first 2 weeks, automated regression alerts tied to eval prompts
- Canary to general availability once manual review and metrics pass thresholds

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to run abstractive summarizer? Hosted vs dedicated vs client-side tiny model. Latency/cost tradeoffs. Could offer two modes: cheap server-side small model v fast (but lower quality) and premium (larger model).
- How to guarantee privacy / PII handling? compression may produce hallucinations; need to mark/blacklist PII and optionally scrub during compression. Integration with KMS for private deployments.
- Backwards compatibility with existing session tokens and prefix cache. Will compressed_blob be cache-key aware? Need to design deterministic expansion for cache hits.

Edge cases & constraints to call out:
- Never compress within code fences, tables, legal disclaimers (configurable)
- Handle multi-party threads (maintain speaker attributions)
- Preserve explicit user-provided facts (e.g., "My account number is 123") if policy says so (must be opt-in for security)

Quick experiment plan (this week):
- Friday: wire up a quick endpoint that runs extractive TF-IDF -> call a small Llama2-7B instruct container to produce 120-token summary, return compressed_blob as JSON.zip. No SDK work, just raw endpoint to demo to Hanae/Marco.
- Next week: run 50 internal sessions through it, measure token counts and response latency when we replay with expand-and-generate stub (fake expand = insert summary as system prompt).

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- TODO: create JIRA INF-4521 and link design doc to Confluence page (placeholder done)
- TODO: add a short eval prompt set for support/tutor/writing (need 60 prompts each)
- TODO: ask infra about storage cost for compressed blobs (should be tiny but check S3 lifecycle for old blobs)
- TODO: grooming session with Hanae (Wed)

References / inspirations:
- Prior art: "Context Distillation" papers, MemNN style condensed memory, commercial features like "context snapshots" we've seen in competitor docs
- Internal notes: see GH PR above for a prototype summarizer used in other experiments

Rough acceptance criteria for MVP:
- APIs implemented and documented in SDK (python + node)
- Compression yields >=2.5x token reduction on 50%+ of sessions without >5% functional regressions on eval set
- Instrumentation for tracking savings and QA alerts in console

Random thoughts (parking lot):
- Could expose a server-side 'summary lens' where user can click to expand older compressed context in UI (nice for debugging and support workflows)
- Could combine with embeddings storage to run cheap similarity search and rehydrate only matching anchors instead of full expansion

End of scratchpad. Keep it messy — this is notes-to-self. Will refine into PRD if prototype numbers look good.
